cards.title: Network Delay Time
cards.problemStatement:
You are given a network of n nodes, labeled from 1 to n. You are also given times, a list of travel times as directed edges times[i] = (ui, vi, wi), where ui is the source node, vi is the target node, and wi is the time it takes for a signal to travel from source to target.

We will send a signal from a given node k. Return the minimum time it takes for all the n nodes to receive the signal. If it is impossible for all the n nodes to receive the signal, return -1.

examples.explanation: The signal reaches nodes 2, 1, 3, and 4 at times 0, 1, 1, and 2 respectively.
The signal reaches node 2 at time 1.
Node 1 cannot be reached from node 2.

constraints: All the pairs (ui, vi) are unique. (i.e., no multiple edges.)

solutions.solutionDescription: Use Dijkstra's algorithm with a min heap to find shortest paths from source node k to all other nodes. Process nodes in order of increasing distance, relaxing edges to update shortest distances. The maximum distance among all reachable nodes is the answer.
solutions.timeComplexityExplanation: Each edge is processed once and heap operations take O(log V) time. With E edges and V vertices, total is O(E log V).
solutions.spaceComplexityExplanation: We store the adjacency list (O(E)) and use a heap and visited set (O(V)).

solutions.solutionDescription: Use SPFA (Bellman-Ford optimization with queue) to find shortest paths. Maintain a queue of nodes to process and update distances when shorter paths are found. Unlike Dijkstra, allows revisiting nodes for better paths.
solutions.timeComplexityExplanation: Average case is O(V+E) when graph is sparse. Worst case is O(V*E) for dense graphs with negative cycles.
solutions.spaceComplexityExplanation: We store the adjacency list (O(E)), distance map (O(V)), and queue (O(V)).

solutions.solutionDescription: Relax all edges V-1 times to find shortest paths from source node k. In each iteration, update distances by checking if path through each edge offers improvement. Works with negative weights and detects negative cycles.
solutions.timeComplexityExplanation: We perform V-1 iterations, and in each iteration we process all E edges.
solutions.spaceComplexityExplanation: We only store a distance array of size V (number of vertices).

solutions.solutionDescription: Compute all-pairs shortest paths using dynamic programming. For each intermediate node, check if going through that node provides a shorter path between any pair of nodes. After processing, extract shortest paths from source k.
solutions.timeComplexityExplanation: We have three nested loops over all V vertices to compute all-pairs shortest paths.
solutions.spaceComplexityExplanation: We use a 2D distance matrix of size V x V.

solutions.solutionDescription: Use DFS to explore all paths from source node k, tracking minimum time to reach each node. Only recurse if current path offers better time than previously recorded. After DFS completes, return maximum distance among all reachable nodes.
solutions.timeComplexityExplanation: In worst case, we may visit each vertex through multiple paths, leading to V*E complexity.
solutions.spaceComplexityExplanation: We store the adjacency list (O(E)) and recursion stack can go up to O(V) depth.
